campaign_spec.critical_open_problem: Does large-scale ordering depend primarily on the directional asymmetry of the orientation reference -(i_a) rather than node-level relational asymmetry?

hypothesis.statement: Large-scale ordering fields arise from the directional asymmetry of local orientation references -(i_a), which act as a relational compass for admissible continuation. This mechanism is independent of node-level relational asymmetry and is sustained by recursive residue inscription.

test_design.description: Systematically vary orientation coherence and reference asymmetry while maintaining relational symmetry.

tests.name: Orientation Coherence Sweep
tests.description: Measure ordering metric as local -(i_a) references transition from random (symmetric entropy) to aligned (asymmetric field), while relations remain symmetric.

tests.name: Symmetric Substrate Persistence
tests.description: Demonstrate stable ordering in a 1,000,000 triad system with perfect relational symmetry but coherent orientation references.

vectors.name: Orientation Symmetry Attack
vectors.attack: Replace the directional (vector) reference -(i_a) with a non-directional (scalar/symmetric) reference.
vectors.failure_condition: Ordering fields survive the loss of reference directionality.
vectors.implication: Asymmetric orientation is not the primary driver.

vectors.name: Asymmetric Relational Noise
vectors.attack: Maximize node-level relational asymmetry but scramble orientation references.
vectors.implication: Relational asymmetry is the true driver, contradicting the current hypothesis.

vectors.name: Residue-Orientation Decoupling
vectors.attack: Maintain orientation alignment but disable residue-conditioned cost reduction.
vectors.failure_condition: Ordering remains stable and persistent over long time-scales.
vectors.implication: Orientation alignment is sufficient without recursive residue stabilization.

maximum_supported_claim.statement: Large-scale ordering fields are causally driven by the directional asymmetry of orientation references; relational asymmetry is an emergent byproduct of the orientation-selection process.
